title: 赠从弟·其二
author: 刘桢
intro: Eight short lines about a pine tree standing straight in a howling mountain wind — written to encourage a younger cousin to stay upright whatever life throws at him.
analysis: 这是刘桢写给堂弟的诗，全诗只写一棵松树。开头两句先画出画面：山上一棵高高挺立的松树，山谷里刮着瑟瑟的冷风。“风声一何盛，松枝一何劲”，两个“一何”（多么）连用，风越猛，越显出松枝的刚劲。接着把时间拉长：冰霜最凄冷的时候，松树一年到头都是端端正正的样子。最后诗人自问自答：难道松树不受严寒之苦吗？不，是因为松柏天生就有这样的本性。这种写法叫“托物言志”——借写一样东西，表达做人的志向。诗人没有直接说“你要坚强”，而是让堂弟从松树身上看到应该怎样做人：在困难和压力面前保持正直，不改变自己。孔子说过“岁寒，然后知松柏之后凋也”，这首诗正是这句话的诗意表达。
analysisEn: Liu Zhen wrote this for his younger cousin, and the whole poem is about a single pine tree. The first two lines set the scene: a tall pine standing straight on a mountain, a cold wind moaning through the valley below. Then comes a pair of exclamations — “how loud the wind! how strong the branches!” — and the harder the wind blows, the tougher the pine looks. Next the poem stretches across a whole year: even when ice and frost are at their bitterest, the pine stays upright from season to season. Finally the poet asks a question and answers it himself: doesn’t the pine suffer in the deep cold? Of course it does — but standing firm is simply its nature. This technique is called tuō wù yán zhì, “using an object to express an ideal”: you describe a thing, and let it speak for what you believe. The poet never says “be strong”. He lets his cousin see in the pine how a person should live — keeping straight under pressure, never bending to circumstances. Confucius once said that only in the cold of winter do we see that pines and cypresses are the last to fade; this poem turns that saying into a picture.
background: Liu Zhen (?–217) was one of the “Seven Masters of the Jian’an Era”, the circle of poets around Cao Cao and his sons, and was known for his proud, upright character. He wrote three poems for his cousin, each using a different image — duckweed, pine, and phoenix; this is the second.
pronunciation: 从弟 cóng dì（堂弟）；瑟瑟 sè sè；一何劲 jìng（不读 jìn）；罹 lí（遭受）；“一何”的“一”按本调标 yī。
version: 采用统编教材（八年级上册“课外古诗词诵读”）文本，全诗八句，网站一联一行（共四行）。

lines.zh: 亭亭山上松，瑟瑟谷中风。
lines.rhythm: 亭亭/山上松，瑟瑟/谷中风
lines.py: tíng tíng shān shàng sōng, sè sè gǔ zhōng fēng
lines.lit: Tall and upright, the pine on the mountain; whistling and cold, the wind in the valley.
lines.en: A pine stands tall on the mountain; a cold wind moans through the valley.

lines.zh: 风声一何盛，松枝一何劲！
lines.rhythm: 风声/一何盛，松枝/一何劲
lines.py: fēng shēng yī hé shèng, sōng zhī yī hé jìng
lines.lit: How mighty the sound of the wind! How sturdy the pine branches!
lines.en: How fierce the wind’s roar — and how tough the pine’s branches!

lines.zh: 冰霜正惨凄，终岁常端正。
lines.rhythm: 冰霜/正惨凄，终岁/常端正
lines.py: bīng shuāng zhèng cǎn qī, zhōng suì cháng duān zhèng
lines.lit: Ice and frost are at their most bitter; all year round it stays upright.
lines.en: When ice and frost are at their cruelest, it stands straight all year long.

lines.zh: 岂不罹凝寒？松柏有本性。
lines.rhythm: 岂不/罹凝寒，松柏/有本性
lines.py: qǐ bù lí níng hán, sōng bǎi yǒu běn xìng
lines.lit: Does it not suffer the frozen cold? Pines and cypresses have their own nature.
lines.en: Doesn’t it feel the freezing cold? It does — but a pine is made to stand firm.

words.note: 现代汉语有“亭亭玉立”，形容女子或花木修长美好。
今天也用来形容冷得发抖，如“瑟瑟发抖”。
古汉语感叹词，相当于现代汉语的“多么”。
读 jìng，如“刚劲”“强劲”；读 jìn 时是“力气”，如“有劲儿”。
现代汉语有“凄惨”，意思偏向悲惨。
岁：年。现代汉语说“一年到头”。
现代汉语仍用，如“端正态度”“五官端正”。
现代书面语有“罹难”“罹患”。
现代汉语仍用，如“本性难移”。

imagery.name: 松
imagery.zh: 松树是全诗的主角，象征坚贞正直、在逆境中不改本色的人格，诗人借它勉励堂弟。
imagery.en: The pine is the hero of the poem — a picture of someone who stays upright under pressure, held up as a model for the cousin.

imagery.name: 风
imagery.zh: 山谷里猛烈的寒风代表外界的压力和打击，风越猛越显出松的刚劲。
imagery.en: The fierce valley wind stands for outside pressure; the harder it blows, the stronger the pine looks.

imagery.name: 霜
imagery.zh: 冰霜写环境最严酷的时候，衬托松树一年到头的端正。
imagery.en: Ice and frost mark the harshest times, which only show off how straight the pine stands all year.
